title: Dilucidationes super methodo elegantissima, qua illustris de la Grange usus est in integranda aequatione differentiali dx/√X = dy/√Y

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Euler is explaining Lagrange's method for integrating the Euler addition equation dx/√X = dy/√Y with X = A+Bx+Cx²+Dx³+Ex⁴ and Y the same polynomial in y. After the quadratic case in §34, this page begins the general 'Analysis' for the quartic.

§35. Euler introduces an auxiliary parameter t with dx/dt = √X and dy/dt = √Y, so ẋ² = X and ẏ² = Y. He sets p = x+y and q = x−y. Since dx² − dy² = dp·dq, this gives ṗq̇ = X − Y = B(x−y) + C(x²−y²) + D(x³−y³) + E(x⁴−y⁴).

§36. Substituting x = (p+q)/2 and y = (p−q)/2 gives X − Y = Bq + Cpq + ¼Dq(3p²+q²) + ½Epq(p²+q²). Dividing by q gives ṗq̇/q = B + Cp + ¼D(3p²+q²) + ½Ep(p²+q²).

§37. Differentiating ẋ² = X with respect to t gives 2ẍ = X'(x), and likewise 2ÿ = Y'(y). Adding, 2p̈ = X'+Y' = 2B + 2Cp + (3/2)D(p²+q²) + Ep(p²+3q²).

On the next page Euler subtracts the two equations: p̈ − ṗq̇/q = ½Dq² + Epq². Dividing by q² gives d/dt(ṗ/q) ... after multiplying by 2ṗ: d[(ṗ/q)²] = (D+2Ep)dp. Integrating, ṗ/q = √(Δ+Dp+Ep²), which is Lagrange's algebraic integral (√X+√Y)/(x−y) = √(Δ + D(x+y) + E(x+y)²).

The method treats the separated equation as the motion of two coordinates in a 'time' t. It is Lagrange's 1766–69 dynamical trick, here re-derived systematically by Euler.
errors: §36, after dividing by q: the printed term '+½Epq(pp+qq)' should be '+½Ep(pp+qq)'. The q was not removed. Euler uses the correct form in the subtraction on the next page, so this is only a misprint.
§37: 'dX = X'dx et dX = Y'dy' should read 'dX = X'dx et dY = Y'dy' (misprint).
§37: in 'erit X''+Y'' the first prime is doubled; it should be X'+Y' (misprint or print defect).

§37: the printed '2ddx/dt² = X'' is correct only in the sense that ddx means d(dx) with dt held constant. All other algebra on the page checks: x³−y³ = ¼q(3p²+q²), x⁴−y⁴ = ½pq(p²+q²), x²+y² = ½(p²+q²), x³+y³ = ¼p(p²+3q²).

ideas.what: Introduce a time parameter t so that ẋ = √X and ẏ = √Y, then pass to the sum and difference coordinates p = x+y, q = x−y, and combine the first-order relation ṗq̇ = X−Y with the second-order relation 2p̈ = X'+Y' to obtain an exact integrable combination.
ideas.modern_name: Lagrange's dynamical method for the Euler addition theorem (first integral of an auxiliary mechanical system; algebraic form of the elliptic addition law)
ideas.usually_credited_to: J.-L. Lagrange, Miscellanea Taurinensia IV (1766–69); Euler's exposition in E506
ideas.where_published: E506 itself (Acta Acad. Sci. Petropol. 1778, publ. 1781); also discussed in later Euler papers on elliptic integrals

ideas.what: Algebraic reduction of X−Y and X'+Y' to the symmetric variables p, q, with division by q.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a faithful expository reworking of Lagrange's well-known method, which is explicitly credited to him and documented in the histories of elliptic integrals. The only findings are minor misprints.
transcription_corrections: §37: the image reads 'erit X''+Y'' (a doubled prime on X), not 'X' + Y''.
The transcription correctly reproduces the printed misprints '½Epq(pp+qq)' in the divided equation and 'dX = Y'dy'. These are errors in the original print, not in the transcription.
